note: Machine-readable record of who wrote each English string in src/i18n/engine/. "upstream" is FreeKill's own en_US, inherited verbatim and not ours to review. "authored" was translated from the Chinese for this project. "override" replaces an upstream entry that was not English (Chinese text, or a placeholder stub). A native-speaker review only needs the "authored", "override" and "mobile" lists. "mobile" is the 249-character packages/mobile roster, translated for this project; upstream ships an en_US stub for it whose values are Chinese, so almost none of it could be inherited. "mobileUncertain" is the subset a translator flagged as ambiguous rather than guessing, and "mobileUntranslated" is what is still missing and falls back to the engine Chinese. "modes" are engine keys this repo's own packages/webmodes defines; they are authored too, but upstream zh_CN does not contain them, so they are listed apart from the zhKeys accounting.

'result differs from every other judgement result in this process' does not say in what respect they must differ (suit, number, or color).
Skill name is the opaque compound 'chi-ye' (kite/owl + choke/sob) with no rules text, and the referenced skill 'pojun' is defined outside this chunk, so neither English name can be pinned down.

Hinges on the mobile-game keyword beishui (last-stand, 'you may beishui' when both Karma colours are equal and above 1); its mechanical effect is defined nowhere in the chunk or repo, so the limited skill is left unrendered rather than guessed.
The Chinese states the cost of 背水 (lose X HP, X = number of prior desperate stands) but never says what it buys - probably an extra use beyond the twice-per-turn cap, but that is not written.

Final clause is ambiguous: the referent of 'target player' (target of which card?) and exactly which of their hand cards counts as 'gained after Honey Gathering at game start' cannot be determined from the text.
Unclear what a card of the same name is named after - the removed Preparation mark, or some card not identified anywhere in this text.

The third option 'Backwater/Last Stand: reduce 1 max HP' states only a cost with no stated benefit - cannot tell if it is a standalone option, an extra cost on option 2, or a way to exceed the once-per-turn limit.

The Chinese writes the target as the slash pair 上家/下家 (previous/next player) three times without saying whether the direction is fixed, chosen by the user, or inherited by the chained Slash, so the chain's direction cannot be pinned down.

Cannot resolve what it reduces: Esteemed Valor's own text has no card-type restriction on discarding, and 友武将 could mean Friend-prefix characters or simply allied characters, which changes X materially.

The referent of the pronoun for the opposing player is unclear: it could be the target of the Troop-Slash, or the player whose card the Troop-Dodge responded to, and for a multi-target Slash it is undefined which target is meant.

Hinges on the card-category term zhinang ('wisdom bag') that the target draws from the pile: it is either a distinct card class in the Opening Stratagems pack or a variant spelling of jinnang (trick card), and the two readings give materially different rules.
The [chara] type means the mark displays a character; unclear whether Fengjie is a place name, a courtesy name, or the phrase meaning to uphold one's charge.
Mark label for an unidentified skill; cannot tell what the mark counts or tracks, so a name would be a guess.
裁裘 literally means cutting a fur robe, but I cannot identify the owning skill, so I cannot tell what the per-round counter actually tracks.
Single-character mark 备 with no context: could mean a reserve/prepared token or be short for a proper name, and Wang Ling's skill is not in this chunk.
The source says the cards are used 'as the corresponding card' but gives no suit-to-card mapping, and leaves the extra effect for playing two cards unspecified.
决进 says HP is set to 1 and converted into armour, without saying what is converted - the excess HP, or the whole HP total; the skill has no rules-text key in this chunk to disambiguate.
Subtitle 日奋金丝 is an obscure allusion; cannot resolve what the golden thread refers to, so any rendering would be a guess.
The subtitle turns on whether the second character is a deliberate homophone pun for eye (Cao Xing shot out Xiahou Dun's eye) or literally means clear sky, which gives two very different readings.
The first two characters are an obscure classical compound whose sense (submitting/spreading influence over Yuyuan, Li Yi's home county) cannot be pinned down confidently.
Subtitle 独计击流 is an obscure allusion; unclear whether 流 names Sun Ce, roving bandits, or something else.
